artists.biography: Terrorvision are an English rock band. They were formed in 1987 (originally as The Spoilt Bratz) in Keighley, and initially disbanded in 2001. The band used Bradford as a base after the name change to Terrorvision, by which time the band members had left home and all moved there.

perplexity.description:
How to Make Friends and Influence People is the second studio album by British rock band Terrorvision, originally released in April 1994 on Total Vegas Recordings. The album is rooted in glam rock and hard rock, showcasing a more confident and musically varied sound compared to their debut. Produced by Gil Norton, known for his work with Pixies and Echo & The Bunnymen, the record features energetic tracks like "Alice What's the Matter," "Oblivion," and "Pretend Best Friend," which highlight the band's knack for catchy riffs and playful, sometimes irreverent lyrics. The album's title is a nod to Dale Carnegie's self-help classic, reflecting its tongue-in-cheek attitude.

In Terrorvision's discography, How to Make Friends and Influence People marked a turning point, establishing the band as a major force in the UK rock scene. It was preceded by the breakthrough success of the single "My House" and followed by several Top 40 singles, including "Oblivion" and "Middleman." The album spent six weeks in the UK Top 40 and helped the band win the Kerrang! Award for Best Newcomer in 1994. Critics praised its fun, accessible energy, with NME awarding it a 7/10, and it remains regarded as one of Terrorvision's most consistent and enjoyable releases.
